notes: One principal object: a role, with login as an attribute of its form. Its system attributes (SUPERUSER, CREATEDB, ...) are fields of the role form, not grants, so no system_privileges source is declared. Membership options inherit and set are provider version-gated. Object privileges: GRANT and REVOKE are provider operations on the privilege kind (tested live on PostgreSQL 18.3 for every object family). The provider carries an object's ACL on the object itself, a NULL ACL is reported as the family's default (flagged privileges_default, since NULL means the owner holds everything, not that nobody does), and column grants sit on the column resources. A function's revoke prefill does not carry its argument types, so an overloaded name is refused by the server rather than guessed. Status stays draft: the provider tree is a per-server opt-in and the inherited tree still serves PostgreSQL registrations, so the legacy host must not refuse them until a browser click-through on the provider tree has been done.
